problem_text:
A logistics manager is assembling a shipment of specialized equipment for a remote research expedition. The manager must select a combination of components to maximize the total utility score while adhering to a strict total mass limit for the transport vehicle.

The components available are:
* Component A: mass 10kg, utility 105 units
* Component B: mass 36kg, utility 138 units
* Component C: mass 35kg, utility 23 units
* Component D: mass 12kg, utility 129 units
* Component E: mass 47kg, utility 223 units
* Component F: mass 46kg, utility 90 units
* Component G: mass 16kg, utility 296 units
* Component H: mass 9kg, utility 96 units
* Component I: mass 48kg, utility 136 units
* Component J: mass 34kg, utility 163 units
* Component K: mass 46kg, utility 20 units
* Component L: mass 47kg, utility 245 units
* Component M: mass 13kg, utility 41 units
* Component N: mass 27kg, utility 95 units
* Component O: mass 25kg, utility 268 units
* Component P: mass 25kg, utility 118 units

Furthermore, due to compatibility requirements, exactly one of Component A and Component B must be included in the shipment.

If Component C is selected, it necessitates a bulky support frame that reduces the effective cargo capacity of the vehicle by 10 kg.
The vehicle can transport a maximum aggregate mass of 333 kg. The manager must determine the optimal selection of components.
